## Pull request overview

Fixes ObjectGrid’s inline-data mode to still load `objectSchema` so column type resolution (and thus CellRenderer selection) remains type-aware even when `data.provider === 'value'`.

**Changes:**
- Added a dedicated `useEffect` to fetch `objectSchema` when inline data is provided (while still skipping `find()`).
- Enhanced the legacy “no columns provided” inline-data fallback to enrich columns using `objectSchema` metadata (types, labels, options, alignment, renderers).
- Added regression tests covering inline data + DataSource for string[], ListColumn[], and legacy fallback column generation paths.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 2 out of 2 changed files in this pull request and generated 2 comments.

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| packages/plugin-grid/src/ObjectGrid.tsx | Fetches schema for inline data and enriches legacy inline-derived columns for type-aware rendering. |
| packages/plugin-grid/src/__tests__/objectdef-enrichment.test.tsx | Adds inline-data regression tests ensuring schema fetch occurs and typed renderers/labels are applied without calling `find()`. |

In this legacy inline-data fallback, the logic for enriching columns (fieldDef lookup, resolvedType, fieldMeta, option generation, alignment, CellRenderer wiring) is effectively duplicated from the string[] column path above. Duplicating this in two places risks the paths diverging over time; consider extracting a shared helper (e.g., buildEnrichedColumnForField) and reusing it in both branches.
